DEP-003.how: lib/install.js no longer prints an outcome it never checked. The unconditional `console.log('  launchctl    loaded')` that sat one line below the `load failed` catch is gone, and so is the unconditional `return true`. The launchctl work moved into an exported `reloadLaunchAgent()` that unloads, loads, and then asks launchd what actually happened via `launchctl list com.interstice.daemon` (new `launchAgentJob()` and `parseLaunchctlList()`). It returns a pid only when launchd is really running the job; install() prints `launchctl    NOT loaded: <detail>` and returns false otherwise. bin/interstice.js now takes install()'s return value and exits 1 with a message instead of printing 'Now run: interstice doctor'. One detail the audit's proposed fix got wrong for this machine: it asked for 'a pid and exit status 0'. The real agent here reports `LastExitStatus = 9` next to a live `PID` because KeepAlive restarted it, so requiring a zero exit status would have called a healthy daemon broken. LastExitStatus is therefore only reported when there is no pid, and the reason is written into the comment above parseLaunchctlList.
DEP-003.verified: Six new tests in test/install.test.js drive reloadLaunchAgent with a stub exec over every branch (load throws, load succeeds but the label is absent, loaded with no PID, loaded with a PID, plus the parser against the real dictionary this machine prints). `node --test test/install.test.js` -> 'tests 14 / pass 14 / fail 0'. Against the real launchd, read only: `node -e "import('./lib/install.js').then(async m=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(await m.launchAgentJob()))})"` -> {"loaded":true,"pid":77971,"lastExitStatus":9}, and the same call with label com.interstice.nosuch -> {"loaded":false,"pid":null,"lastExitStatus":null}. The operator's daemon on 7420 was never unloaded or restarted.

DEP-010.how: Step (b) of the reload contract now exists in both places. In lib/install.js, after `launchctl list` reports a pid, install() polls GET /api/health (new `daemonPidOnPort()` and `waitForDaemon()`, sending the x-interstice-token header) and requires the pid in the health response to EQUAL the pid launchd reported. Same number or it is not the agent's process, which is precisely the hole the row named: a hand-started foreground daemon answers /api/health exactly as well as the agent does. install() returns false and prints which pid actually holds the port when they differ. In lib/doctor.js a new check, 'the LaunchAgent is loaded, not merely present', sits between 'LaunchAgent installed' (plist on disk) and 'the daemon is answering right now' (something on the port) and asks launchd directly, then makes the same pid comparison. A loaded-and-running agent, a loaded-but-dead agent, an unloaded agent, and a hand-started daemon squatting the port are now four distinguishable doctor outputs where they used to be one.
DEP-010.verified: `node bin/interstice.js doctor` on the live machine prints, under startup: '✓ the LaunchAgent is loaded, not merely present   pid 77971, and it is the process answering on 7420', next to '✓ the daemon is answering right now   pid 77971, up 7m, 12 gaps this run'. The two pids agreeing is the evidence. Cross checked out of band: `/bin/launchctl list com.interstice.daemon` prints "PID" = 77971, and `curl -s -H "x-interstice-token: $(cat logs/control-token)" http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/health` returns "pid": 77971. The failure directions are covered by the stub-exec tests in test/install.test.js: 'a job that loads but dies on startup is not reported as loaded either' and 'a load launchd accepted but never registered is not reported as loaded'.

DEP-019.how: Added test/server-content-type.test.js, which stands up the REAL createServer from lib/server.js on port 7523 with a stub daemon and a config built from config.defaults(), then reads content-type off real responses. It covers twelve JSON GET routes (/api/health, /api/status, /api/config, /api/gaps, /api/stats, /api/events, /api/queued, /api/panel, /api/focus, /api/cards, /api/stars/day, /api/stars/month), the 400 branch of a POST (POST /api/queued sent empty, so nothing is appended to the real log), the handler's own 400 error shape, the pre-dispatch 401 refusal, and text/html for /, /index.html, /panel and /debug. The route the rule is really about is the fallthrough: /nope, /api/nope and /api/health/extra must each come back 404 application/json with {error:'not found'}, so lib/server.js:601 can never regress into serving dashboard.html. Two routes are deliberately excluded with the reason written in the file: /api/companions takes two real screen captures a second apart, and the remaining POSTs write to logs or open windows. /api/cards is included with a config pointing anki.url at a closed port so it takes its caught-error branch immediately rather than depending on whether Anki is running.

TC-007.how: Both halves. The gate that was aborting every job is gone: .github/workflows/ci.yml no longer runs `test ! -f package-lock.json && echo "zero-dependency by design"`. In its place, 'Install dev dependencies' runs `npm ci` (the repo has a real devDependency, @playwright/test, and a tracked lockfile), and 'No runtime dependencies' asserts the invariant that is still true, that package.json has no `dependencies` at all. Then the count assertion the row asks for: the Test step captures TAP with `node --test --test-reporter=tap | tee /tmp/tap.txt`, reads the executed count out of the '# pass' summary line, echoes it, and requires it to be at least 290. This matters because the runner cannot report a zero-selection as a failure on its own. Playwright decision: CI installs the browser (`npx playwright install chromium`) rather than restricting the run to unit tests, because `node --test` already picks the five test/*.pw.mjs specs up (its default pattern covers all of test/) and they are the only coverage the panel's rendering has; excluding them would have made the count floor green while the panel went untested.

TC-008.how: A literal-detector now ships: scripts/literal-detector.mjs, wired as .githooks/pre-commit (enabled in this clone with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, which is per-clone and so cannot be shipped by the repo alone) and as the CI step 'Assertions carry no bare literals', which is the copy that cannot be skipped. The hook checks only staged files under test/. Two shapes are blocked, drawn narrowly on purpose because a gate that cries wolf gets turned off, and both boundaries are argued in the file header: a DATE literal on the expected side whose exact text also appears on a non-assertion line of the same file (that second occurrence is the fixture, and the pair is what drifts), and a COUNT of 2 or more on the expected side of a .length/.size/count comparison (0 and 1 are shapes, 'nothing came out' and 'exactly one thing came out', not transcriptions of how many rows somebody typed). A date that appears only in the assertion is deliberately NOT flagged: in test/focus-blocks.test.js:83, `assert.equal(out[0].day, '2026-08-20')` against a block started at 23:50 on the 19th, the literal IS the specification, and deriving it from the fixture would mean restating the date arithmetic under test. An escape hatch, a `literal-ok:` comment anywhere in the contiguous comment block above the assertion, covers the rest. The detector then went from 11 findings to 0: derived test/stars-routes.test.js off named DAY/MONTH/STAR constants (the audit's own example: the assertion side had re-typed '2026-08-19' and '2026-08-19T09:00:00-07:00' from the stub two lines up), records.length off targets.length in test/video-probe.test.js, the item cap off a named CAP in test/notes.test.js, the shelf window off READ_AHEAD and KEEP_BEHIND in test/reader-shelf.test.js (whose own comment claimed it was bounded by the configured numbers while asserting a magic 9), the recovered stars off [a, b] and the month filters off named august/september arrays in test/focus-store.test.js, the post-cooldown delivery off beforeLapse + 1 in test/engine.test.js, and the line count off the input's own length in test/ocr.test.js. Two genuine specification literals were marked with reasons rather than mangled: the 64 hex characters of a 32-byte token in test/auth.test.js and the two paragraphs in test/ocr.test.js.

It was failing before the fixes: the same command reported '11 bare literals on the assertion side' listing test/stars-routes.test.js:37 and :39 among them. The hook proven in both directions: staging a probe file containing `assert.equal(FIXTURE[0], '2026-08-19')` and `assert.equal(FIXTURE.length, 2)` made `.githooks/pre-commit` print '2 bare literals on the assertion side' and exit 1; with the probe removed and the real test tree staged it printed 'no bare literals in 10 test files' and exit 0 (probe file moved to ~/.Trash, `git reset` run). `git config --get core.hooksPath` -> '.githooks'. TC-010.how: Both gates can now do both jobs, and each was checked against a known-good tree and a deliberately broken one before being trusted. Gate one, the dependency claim: `test ! -f package-lock.json` could never pass on the repo's intended state, so it is replaced by `npm ci` plus an assertion that package.json declares no runtime `dependencies`, which is true today and false the moment somebody adds one. Gate two, the test run: `node --test` exits 0 on a zero-selection, so the exit code alone could not fail when the thing it guards was broken; the Test step now reads the executed count out of the TAP '# pass' line and requires at least 290. Every automated check introduced by this batch was held to the same standard: the content-type test (DEP-019) was made to fail by breaking the 404 fallthrough, the literal-detector was made to fail by staging a probe file, and the launchctl verification (DEP-003, DEP-010) has stub-exec tests for each of its failure branches as well as its success branch.
